---
title: Make a connector follow changes
description: Teach the reading list connector to archive entries its service drops, then change the list, run it again, and see a failed run reported.
---

- **You'll build** on the connector from [Build a connector](/build/connector). It will archive an entry the service drops, and you'll watch it follow a changed list.
- **You need** that connector, built, with its key, and the reading list service still running. Keep the `marfa-connectors` checkout as your working folder.
- **You'll have** a connector that creates, updates and archives items to match the service, and a failed run you can read on the instance.

<Steps paged>
<Step>

### Set aside what the service dropped

So far the connector only adds and updates. Open `connectors/readlist/src/main.ts`, and ask `run` for two more helpers, `held` and `archive`:

```ts title="connectors/readlist/src/main.ts"
  async run({ env, signal, upsert, held, archive }) {
```

At the end of `run`, after the `upsert`, archive each item whose entry the service no longer lists:

```ts title="connectors/readlist/src/main.ts"
    const listed = new Set(entries.map((entry) => key(entry.id)));
    const gone = (await held(readlistEntry.id))
      .map((row) => row.source_id)
      .filter((id): id is string => id !== undefined && !listed.has(id));
    await archive(readlistEntry.id, gone);
```

`held` answers the items the connector wrote. Reading a missing entry as deleted is safe here because **this service lists every entry it has**; [Pull and push](/build/connector-pull-and-push#set-aside-what-the-vendor-deleted) covers a vendor that doesn't.

Build again:

```bash
pnpm build
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Change the list

In the `reading-list` folder, change `entries.json`: retitle entry 1, delete entry 2, and add entry 3.

```json title="reading-list/entries.json"
[
  {
    "id": "1",
    "title": "The Pragmatic Programmer, 20th anniversary edition",
    "url": "https://example.com/pragmatic",
    "author": "Hunt and Thomas",
    "added": "2026-09-01T09:00:00Z"
  },
  {
    "id": "3",
    "title": "Designing Data-Intensive Applications",
    "url": "https://example.com/ddia",
    "author": "Kleppmann",
    "added": "2026-10-02T07:15:00Z"
  }
]
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Run it again

Run the connector with the same command as before, using the connector's key. Its report counts one entry of each kind:

<Terminal>

```bash
MARFA_API_URL=http://localhost:8600 \
MARFA_API_KEY=<the connector's key> \
READLIST_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4100 \
READLIST_TOKEN=demo-token \
node connectors/readlist/dist/main.js --once
```

```text
2026-10-21T15:34:24.816Z info registered as 01a15f19-6d25-7806-8fd1-226237a916c5
2026-10-21T15:34:24.883Z info run succeeded: created 1, updated 1, archived 1, unchanged 0, skipped 0
```

</Terminal>

List the items in every state, with your own key, to see the archived one too:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa items list --type readlist.entry --state any
```

```text
01a15f19-6f60-799a-bccf-49486b3d0b19  readlist.entry  2026-10-02T07:15:00.000Z  Designing Data-Intensive Applications
01a15f19-6d82-79db-9eb9-e662460ad766  readlist.entry  2026-09-03T18:30:00.000Z  A Philosophy of Software Design                     [archived]
01a15f19-6d7e-7700-bb96-225106877d41  readlist.entry  2026-09-01T09:00:00.000Z  The Pragmatic Programmer, 20th anniversary edition
```

</Terminal>

The retitled entry kept its ID and moved to version 2. The new entry is a new item, and the dropped one is **archived, not deleted**, so it keeps its history. Run the connector once more without changing the list, and its report counts every entry `unchanged`.

</Step>
<Step>

### See a run fail

Run the connector with a token the service refuses. The service answers `401`, and the run fails:

<Terminal>

```bash
MARFA_API_URL=http://localhost:8600 \
MARFA_API_KEY=<the connector's key> \
READLIST_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4100 \
READLIST_TOKEN=wrong-token \
node connectors/readlist/dist/main.js --once
```

```text
2026-10-21T15:34:25.323Z info registered as 01a15f19-6d25-7806-8fd1-226237a916c5
2026-10-21T15:34:25.355Z error run failed: the reading list answered 401; created 0, updated 0, archived 0, unchanged 0, skipped 0
```

</Terminal>

The instance keeps the failure on the connector's registration, with its error:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa connectors list
```

```text
01a15f19-6d25-7806-8fd1-226237a916c5  readlist  readlist  failed  2026-10-21T15:34:25.355Z  the reading list answered 401
```

</Terminal>

**Nothing it wrote before is lost**, and the next run with the right token reads the whole list again.

</Step>
</Steps>

## Next steps

You have a connector that keeps your instance in step with a vendor and reports each run. Stop the reading list service with Control-C when you're done.

This connector only reads. Edit an entry's title in Marfa, and the next run puts the service's title back, with a warning that names the field. To carry changes back to the vendor, or to act on its webhooks, go on to the connector guides:
